2019-03-05 11:17:46	Oh! Easy peasy: mix up oil, salt, spices (turmeric, chilli, cumin, paprika/whatever takes your fancy), and spread over cauliflower. Roast at about 200 degrees until tender (this raises quite a while and you'll want to cover the cauli with foil after it has browned off). Meanwhile, make hummus with chickpeas, tahini, garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, water. When the cauli comes out of oven, spread with hummus and sprinkle perils of half a pomegranate over the top. Serve with green salad and pita bread. Nom!

HISTORICAL FACT: Papen’s Marburg speech was Sunday, 17 June 1934. Hitler managed to fit in a rebuttal on the same day. Papen goes to Hitler on Wednesday, 20 June 1934, complains that interference from Geobbels (‘a junior minister’) is intolerable, threatens to resign but w/draws resignation at Hitler’s request. Hitler (IMHO) sees that if Papen (who is VC) takes his complaint to Hg, it might be enough to push him (Hg) into declaring martial law. Hitler flies to Neudeck the following day, promises Hg that he will deal with SA (which he does by way NOLK). Hg, conveniently, dies on 2 Aug. Hitler becomes Pres and thus Head of Government and Head of State.
PLUME FICTION: Papen goes to Hitler on Wednesday, 20 June 1934, resigns and does not w/draw. He leaves Chancellery and drives straight-away to Neudeck (instead of hanging around Berlin pouting). I have added a fictional element to the story which convinces Hg next stop anarchy so he declares martial law. Hitler’s plane is met by army detachment posing as SS. Hitler is taken into custody and spirited off to ? Military coup ensues.
I chose the period after Marburg but before NOLK while Hg was still alive because that was the very last chance that anyone had to stop Hitler and Hg was the only person with the constitutional power to do it. He had threatened martial law several times before that time, and had no time for Hitler but even less time for arbitrary use of Presidential power.

2024-01-19 19:14:21	iZZ plant Zamioculcas zamifolia is a beautiful leafy plant with interesting thick, glossy green leaves. While the ZZ plant can be grown outdoors, it makes a fantastic almost unkillable indoor plant. It’s been described as the ultimate indoor plant because of its tolerance to low light and lack of water. In the wild it survives drought periods by disappearing almost completely and then resprouting from its underground, potatolike tubers when the rains eventually come. So, in the unlikely event that your ZZ plant appears to have died, a good drink just might encourage it to start developing new shoots. iId

Not that git also has an ‘ignore’ function for files  e.g. when I compile stuff, the compiled stuff is always ignored as it is always generated from the source code and git does not handle binary files very well  so normally one avoids pushing compiled files, .exe files, .zip files, into git and instead, push the source code plus any scripts or make files or whathaveyou to derive the binary files from the source code.iI,

2024-08-07 08:53:23	\The point of dual TMs is not the same as dual backup drives. Both TMs should be connected to the Mac, and ‘live’. Mac OS X will understand what we’re doing and make BOTH drives a complete TM backup. It will backup to drive 1 at 1000, to drive 2 at 1030, to drive 1 at 1100 or something like that. Both drive 1 and drive 2 are fully selfcontained Time Machine backups and should one die, the other might be at most 30 mins out of date, but apart from that it’s complete. That’s protection against a TM drive failing  but not when the house burns down.Having dual backup drives and storing one physically in a different location is a different thing  you should do that too. I used to use Carbon Copy Cloner to make multiple image backups of the computer and store those in other locations. That’s protection against the house burning down.
2024-08-07 08:53:53	JI now use Backblaze for offsite backup, rather than Carbon Copy CloneriIH
2024-08-07 08:56:21	TM is mostly a ‘buttsaver’ for those situations where a wrong move causes an important file to disappear e.g. dragging the wrong file to the Trash and emptying it  I’ve done that many times, or when a Mac needs to be reinstalled from scratch and restored.

2025-03-05 07:21:06	That makes sense  192.168.1.254 is your internet gateway, not your PC, hence the 254 which is common for internet gateways  they’re often ‘1’ or ‘254’. You need to connect to 192.168.1.67 and not to 192.168.1.254. Also, if the PC does not respond to pings that might indicate the PC’s firewall is up. On the Mac, try running `ifconfig` from a Terminal window  it should give you a similar address  e.g. 192.168.1.68 or suchlike. Then try ping from a CMD window on the PC to the Mac’s address  blow through the pipe the other way.

2025-05-10 21:44:53	I tend to fence those kinds of things off with a boolean flag e.g a routine ‘SafeOn’ which boils down to ‘if  fEventHandlerEnabled  fEventHandlerEnabled  true On  ’ and SafeOff which boils down to ‘if fEventHandlerEnabled  Off fEventHandlerEnabled  false ’ so repeated calls to SafeOn or SaveOff are harmless. Something like that. Or sometimes I use a ‘nestLevel’ counter each call to On increments the counter, each call to Off decrements it, and only when the counter transitions from 0 to 1 or 1 to 0 anything happens. All other transitions e.g. 1 to 2 are donothings. So you have to call an equal number of Off to balance a number of calls to On

2026-02-20 17:13:35	Primary Sovereign  Royal TitlesCaliph Khalifa The highest title, meaning ""successor"" to the Prophet Muhammad. Historically, it combined supreme religious and secular authority over the entire Islamic world.Sultan Originally meaning ""authority"" or ""dominion,"" this title was used by independent monarchs of large realms e.g., Sultan of Oman.Malik The literal Arabic word for ""King"" feminine Malika. It is currently used by monarchs in Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Bahrain, and Morocco.Emir Amir Meaning ""commander"" or ""prince."" 2026-02-20 17:17:05	Sufism and Sunni Islam are not separate sects rather, Sufism is the mystical, inner dimension of Islam that exists primarily within the Sunni tradition. While over 95 of Sufis are Sunni, they differ from ""traditional"" or ""reformist"" Sunnis in their focus on spiritual experience over external legalism. Core Differences in FocusMethod of Worship Mainstream Sunnis primarily follow the Sharia outer law focusing on ritual duties and jurisprudence. Sufis also follow Sharia but add a Tariqa inner path, seeking a direct, personal experience of God in this life.Leadership Sunnis generally follow religious scholars Ulama for legal guidance. Sufis pledge allegiance Bay'ah to a spiritual guide, or Sheikh, who is believed to be part of an unbroken chain of transmission back to the Prophet Muhammad.Spiritual Practices Sufis engage in additional rituals such as Dhikr meditative remembrance of God, Muraqaba meditation, and sometimes devotional music or movement, like the ""whirling"" of the Mevlevi order. Relationship  ConflictsAspect Mainstream SunniSufi SunnibasedView of GodTranscendent, Omnipotent, to be met in the Hereafter.Immanent seeks to ""lose oneself"" in the Divine in this life.Saint VenerationGenerally rejected or limited focus on direct prayer to God.Common practice of visiting shrines and seeking blessings Baraka from saints.LegalismHigh emphasis on literal adherence to Hadith and Law.Emphasis on the ""spirit"" of the law and inner purification Tazkiyah.Historically, most major Sunni scholars, such as AlGhazali, were also Sufis, viewing it as the ""science of the heart"". However, modern reformist movements like Salafism and Wahhabism are often critical of Sufism, viewing practices like saint veneration as innovations Bid'ah or even idolatry.
